children: Shares of Suzlon Energy Ltd. recovered from the lows of the day to trade little changed having recovered from the lows of the day on Tuesday, September 8, after bagging its first 200 MW wind energy order from Ayana Renewable Power Ltd.

This is Suzlon's third DevCo-led wind order across two states, Madhya Pradesh and Andhra Pradesh, the company said in its exchange filing. The company also said that this order win has taken the company's overall sale for the flagship S144 3 MW platform past the 10 GW mark.
Suzlon DevCo is an integrated co-development platform, to incubate renewable energy projects three to five years before construction.

As part of the project, Suzlon Energy will install 64 S144 turbines each with a rated capacity of 3.15 MW. The project will be executed through Suzlon's EPC business, which will cover turbine supply, land acquisition, balance of plant, pooling substation, extra high voltage line, commissioning and operations & maintenance services.
The project will be executed in Limbawas in Madhya Pradesh and the power generated will be connected to the MPPCL state grid, Suzlon's statement said.

"With 55 GW+ wind potential at 150 metres, Madhya Pradesh is well positioned to be one of the key states which will drive the next phase of India’s wind energy growth," Suzlon Group Vice Chairman & Co-Founder Girish Tanti said.
Ajay Kapur, the Suzlon Group CEO said that the company is already starting to see the results of their integrated approach to developing renewable energy assets.
Shares of Suzlon Energy are trading little changed at ₹45.59 on Tuesday after the order win announcement. The stock is still down 13% so far this year.

title: Suzlon Energy bags 200 MW order from Ayana Renewable Power; S144 crosses 10 GW in sales
